brief: RBNZ held its cash rate at 2.75%, surprising markets, citing global uncertainty, while flagging conditional tightening risk. Australian trimmed-mean and headline inflation both accelerated (0.8% to 1.0% q/q, 3.6% to 3.7% y/y). RBA's Bullock said upside risks are materialising and inflation will run hotter than the August base case, pushing next week's hike odds to 86% from 60%. Australian front-end futures sold off then partly recovered as the rate strip flattened. US fixed income weakened in the Asia session on the Australian print, a WSJ report that Washington told Gulf states to prepare for a short military campaign after the midterms, an added Patriot deployment to Israel, and a firmer equity tape (Kospi up 6.63% on stronger SK Hynix earnings and a call that Nvidia-linked component shortages persist to 2030). Fed-day options flow skewed to downside puts (TYZ6, weekly TY) despite one bullish SFRF7 call ladder. CTAs stayed heavily short duration, with partial short covering in Japan and Australia, and credit positioning flipped from long liquidation to outright shorts, with US IG the exception. UBS economics expects no Fed hike, two possible dissenters, and a brief, data-trend-framed Warsh press conference. The 5y auction tailed for a 12th straight time despite a stronger indirect bid.
